jokes.punchline: Instead of the conventional 'I do,' Kip responds 'You know I do' — adding unsolicited emphasis that implies the officiant should obviously already know the answer, delivered with Kip's characteristic mild smugness
jokes.explanation: Four words, enormous character comedy. 'You know I do' implies Kip is slightly offended that anyone would question his devotion to Lafawnduh — as if the entire formal ceremony is an unnecessary formality given how obviously in love he is. It's also mildly rude to the officiant. The confidence is completely at odds with Kip's established awkwardness, but in a way that makes it funnier. Comparable to the 8.0 anchor in economy and character specificity. Highly quotable.

jokes.text: Kip's wedding song: '# We met in a chat room / Now our love can fully bloom #'
jokes.setup: Kip performs a song at his wedding reception as a romantic gesture to Lafawnduh
jokes.punchline: The song earnestly celebrates their internet courtship ('we met in a chat room') as if it were a traditional romance — the specificity of 'chat room' in a wedding song is jarring and perfectly Kip
jokes.explanation: One of the great comedy songs in indie film. 'We met in a chat room / now our love can fully bloom' perfectly captures Kip's earnest romanticism about internet culture — he genuinely finds this beautiful. The rhyme ('chat room / fully bloom') is both effortful and terrible, which makes it funnier. The whole song is Kip treating online dating with the reverence of a Homeric epic.

jokes.text: "# But you, you make me 'salvivate' #"
jokes.setup: Kip is singing a romantic song to Lafawnduh at their wedding
jokes.punchline: Kip mispronounces 'salivate' as 'salvivate' in his love song — either a genuine malapropism or a forced rhyme that he doesn't realize is wrong — delivered with complete earnestness
jokes.explanation: A single word doing exceptional comedic work. 'Salvivate' is funnier than 'salivate' would be in a romantic song for two reasons: (1) it's wrong, suggesting Kip either doesn't know the word or is forcing a rhyme, and (2) salivation itself is not typically a romantic sentiment — the fact that Kip thinks this is romantic language is itself funny. The earnestness is everything. This line became a minor cultural touchstone for fans of the film. High marks across the board for a one-word joke.

jokes.text: "# Yes, I love technology / But not as much as you, you see / But I still love technology / Always and forever #"
jokes.setup: Kip is performing a wedding song professing his love for Lafawnduh
jokes.punchline: He interrupts the declaration of love to clarify that he loves technology, then corrects himself to say he loves Lafawnduh more, then immediately re-affirms that he still loves technology — in a song to his new wife
jokes.explanation: One of the great character comedy moments in the film. The structure is a perfect three-step joke: (1) I love technology, (2) but not as much as you — standard romantic qualifier, (3) BUT I STILL LOVE TECHNOLOGY. The third step is the genius move — after the romantic pivot, Kip walks it back to reassure the audience (and himself) that he hasn't abandoned technology entirely. This is performed to Lafawnduh at their wedding. It could ONLY come from Kip. The character integration is perfect: Kip's love of technology, his obliviousness, and his genuine emotion are all in four lines. This is the best joke of the entire reel on craft grounds. Exceeds the 8.0 anchor substantially; approaches the 9.5 anchor in terms of cultural impact. Highly quotable — many fans of the film can recite this.

jokes.text: "Sorry I'm late. I just got done taming a wild honeymoon stallion for you guys."
jokes.setup: Napoleon arrives late to Kip's wedding/reception; he needs to explain his absence
jokes.punchline: His excuse is that he was 'taming a wild honeymoon stallion' — an absurd, implausible, and completely unexplained act that Napoleon delivers as if it's a perfectly normal and considerate thing to do
jokes.explanation: Classic Napoleon logic: he is late, he has an explanation, the explanation raises more questions than it answers, and he seems entirely unbothered by any of this. 'Wild honeymoon stallion' is a perfect Napoleon phrase — 'honeymoon' as an adjective applied to a horse implies a whole absurd chivalric worldview where Napoleon prepared a horse as a wedding gift. 'Taming' implies he went through difficulty for them. The specificity ('wild' + 'honeymoon') elevates it above a generic absurdist excuse. High originality and character integration.

jokes.text: "Hey, Deb, can you take a photo of me on the horse real quick?"
jokes.setup: Napoleon has just presented Kip and Lafawnduh with a horse; this is ostensibly a gift for them
jokes.punchline: Napoleon's first request upon arriving at his brother's wedding — before anything else — is to have his photo taken on the horse. The horse is partly for them, partly for Napoleon.
jokes.explanation: Napoleon's selfishness is completely innocent — he genuinely wants the photo because it would be cool, not to upstage his brother. The 'real quick' implies this is a minor, reasonable request. It's funny because it reveals Napoleon as someone who cannot fully separate himself from any situation. Also works because the reconciliation with Deb is now expressed through asking her for a favor.

jokes.text: "I hope your guys's experiences are unforgettable." / "Lookee, lookee. A little keepsake for you guys."
jokes.setup: Uncle Rico appears at the wedding, apparently uninvited; Kip and Lafawnduh are trying to leave on their honeymoon
jokes.punchline: Rico shows up with a 'keepsake' and the phrasing 'your guys's experiences' — appearing to have inserted himself into a wedding he ruined family relationships to attend, still doing his salesman schtick with the word 'lookee lookee'
jokes.explanation: 'Lookee, lookee' is a Rico-specific verbal tic — the salesman who can't turn it off even at a family wedding. 'A little keepsake' is ominous given Rico's track record. The joke is that Rico has shown up and is still doing his thing, completely unaware or unbothered by the damage he's caused. Character integration is high; the material itself is not especially clever.
